properties.chose: Anthony, 2026-10-12: "Let's go with your suggestions." Kept as intent: (a) a decision that is hard to undo, or that much depends on, is asked what a wrong call costs and how far a right one goes (req:a-hard-to-undo-decision-is-asked-what-a-wrong-call-costs-and-how-far-a-right-one-goes); (b) before a decision is settled, reflow2 shows what undoing it would cost, from the built and checked work downstream (req:a-decision-shows-what-undoing-it-would-cost). Both are cheap, need no schema change and reuse existing reads. (e) is designed together with the deferred via-negativa measure (removals beside additions) as one measure that also counts failures that came back and reversals. (c), convex tinkering as a way to settle, waits until failures actually come back to the record (0 so far). (d), a report of concave exposure across a design, comes later.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (Anthony, 2026-10-12, the second concept from Taleb's Antifragile after via negativa).

His words: "curious if we can somehow introduce convexity into the decision process within reflow2? I think one of the remaining tasks was part (d), but I feel trying to introduce convexity into the decision process of reflow2 will lead to people having better designs."

The concept, as he gave it:
- A convex payoff has a limited downside and an open upside, so it gains from volatility (positive asymmetry).
- A concave payoff has a small steady upside and an open downside, so it loses from volatility (negative asymmetry).
- Jensen's inequality: for a convex function, the average of the outcomes beats the outcome of the average.
- Convex tinkering: trial and error where a failure costs little and a success can be large.

What it means for a design decision, in plain words:
- Convex: cheap to try, cheap to undo if wrong, and it can grow if it works.
- Concave: a small gain if it works, and a large loss that spreads if it is wrong.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HOLDS THAT BEARS ON IT:
- The cost of being wrong is partly structural, and reflow2 can compute it: what hangs off a decision (what_next's shaping band), what a change reaches (propagate_from), and how many layers a change must unpeel (the open cement idea).
- Trying options before committing is half-built: register_alternative forks a decision, analyze_alternatives compares the branches on the same measures, and collapse_decision keeps the losers on the record. The open trial-skill idea names what is missing: no skill drives it end to end, and nothing records what a trial cost.
- Learning from failure needs the failure to reach the record. loop_status reads 78 of 440 checks compared with a real run, and 0 failures ever fed back.

WAYS IT COULD WORK, none chosen:
(a) An advisory question when a decision is settled, barbell-style like the via-negativa rule: asked only for decisions that are hard to undo or that much depends on. "If this is wrong, what does undoing it cost, and is that cost capped? If it is right, how far can it go?"
(b) Show the downside reflow2 can compute. For a decision: how much built and checked work hangs off it, and how many layers a reversal would unpeel. The upside stays the person's judgement; reflow2 never scores it.
(c) Convex tinkering as a way to settle a decision: a small trial with a stated cost cap and a stop rule, run before committing, with its result fed back to the decision. It would be delivered through the alternatives family and the trial-skill idea.
(d) A read of where a design is exposed the concave way: hard-to-undo decisions with a large fan-out, single points of failure, and assumptions many things rest on with no fallback. These are the places where a surprise costs more than in proportion.
(e) Measure whether the design gains from stress: failures fed back, reversals made and what they cost, and removals beside additions (the deferred (d) of the via-negativa idea). Without this, "antifragile" stays a slogan.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-12 — convexity enters the decision process as (a) a barbell question at the hard-to-undo end and (b) the computed cost of undoing a decision; (e) merges with the removals measure; (c) waits for failures to come back; (d) later
properties.rationale:
Counter-arguments and costs, recorded beside the idea, not against it:

1. REFLOW2 CANNOT KNOW THE PAYOFFS. Probabilities and upside are judgements, and a number reflow2 made up would be worse than none. Taleb's own point helps here: you cannot measure the tails, but you can see the SHAPE of your exposure. reflow2 can show the structure of the downside (what hangs off, how hard to undo), never a convexity score as a verdict (dec:report-dont-judge).

2. NOT EVERY DECISION NEEDS IT. A question on every choice becomes noise and teaches people to skip it. Barbell: most decisions are small and reversible and need nothing; the few that are hard to undo get the question (the same shape as the via-negativa rule kept on 2026-10-12).

3. THE WORDS MUST NOT REACH THE USER. "Convex" and "concave" are the lens for this record. A person hears "cheap to undo, big if it works" against "a small win, a big loss if wrong" (the register rule).

4. TINKERING ONLY HELPS IF FAILURES COME BACK. Zero failures fed back means the loop cannot learn from volatility yet. So (e), or the loop-closure work, is a precondition for (c) to be more than a name.

5. OVERLAP. (c) is largely dec:idea-trial-driven-choice-skill and (b) is largely dec:idea-cement-is-measured-as-the-decision-layers-a-change-must-unpeel. This idea is the principle that ties them together, and should not become a second copy of either.

6. PRECEDENT, in systems engineering terms: a likelihood × consequence risk matrix averages and so cannot see asymmetry. Competitive prototyping and a modular open systems approach in acquisition are the convex moves: they keep options open and make a wrong guess cheap.

COSTS: (a) is text in the decision skills plus a release. (b) is a read over what already exists. (c) builds on built tools plus a skill. (d) is a new report. (e) is code and a release, and overlaps the via-negativa measure already on this session's list.
